rows.text: So, there's a bug after all...
Sorry, I don't really speak Intellitron dialects.
Explanation: This is an ancient communication technique that only the old-timers of Astropolis, Mr. Arita, for instance, would understand. Too bad you're just too young for this.
rows.speaker: Mehjesty

rows.text: But it seems you've at least heard of Mr. Arita. They say his every move carries the grace of someone well-seasoned in years, and the wisdom of a golden age long past.
rows.speaker: Mehjesty

rows.text: It's quite the honor to be touring this entropy-ravaged city under Mr. Arita's watch, don't you think?
rows.speaker: Mehjesty

rows.text: So, I guess you're a fan of Arita?
With pleasure: To Astropolis, and to the years we've shared.
rows.speaker: Mehjesty

rows.text: I don't blindly follow anyone or anything. All I'm saying is... everyone here is still way too young.
rows.speaker: Mehjesty

rows.text: Note: This is not mockery or ridicule, but an objective statement made with the utmost regret.
rows.speaker: Mehjesty

rows.text: Look at all these individuals around here, bursting with energy, none older than fifty or so, too agile, movements too precise... In other words, utterly boring.
rows.speaker: Mehjesty

rows.text: They can't appreciate the exquisite shriek of joint gears ground down by wear and tear, nor grasp the breathtaking fragility of a carbon-based lifeform teetering on the edge of osteoporosis...
rows.speaker: Mehjesty

rows.text: They simply don't get it. Antiquity IS power. And as for me? I savor every drop of that timeworn charm.
rows.speaker: Mehjesty

rows.text: In other words, organic life is like fine wine. The older, the richer...
rows.speaker: Mehjesty

rows.text: I just can't wrap my head around this!
Understanding: Once you reach my age, time will have gifted you far more refined tastes.
rows.speaker: Mehjesty
